name: Justice Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public justice and criminal-justice data.

entries.title: BJS National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS)
entries.description: The nation's primary source of information on criminal victimization — a nationally representative household survey on the frequency, characteristics, and consequences of nonfatal personal and household property crimes, including crimes not reported to police.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS)
entries.attribution: Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Crime Victimization Survey
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page calls the NCVS "the nation's primary source of information on criminal victimization", with a yearly sample of "about 240,000 persons in about 150,000 households", and gives the collection period as 1973 – 2024. Public-use microdata is usually archived at ICPSR's National Archive of Criminal Justice Data (NACJD), which returned 403 to curl this session and was not checked. BJS's own data tools publish aggregate tables. The csv format is assumed, not checked.

entries.title: BJS National Prisoner Statistics (NPS)
entries.description: BJS's annual national- and state-level counts of prisoners held in state and federal prison facilities, the basis of the annual Prisoners report series.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS)

coverage.spatial: United States (national and state level; federal system)

entries.attribution: Bureau of Justice Statistics, National Prisoner Statistics program
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The cataloged URL is where the old ...-nps-program URL redirects. The page shows Status: Active, Frequency: Annual, Latest Data Available: 2023, Collection Period: 1926-present, and describes "annual national- and state-level data on the number of prisoners in state and federal prison facilities". The formats are assumed from the BJS report and data-table distribution, not checked.

entries.title: DOJ: First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files (27 February 2025)
entries.description: The Department of Justice and FBI's February 2025 release of the "first phase" of declassified Epstein files: an evidence list, flight logs previously released in U.S. v. Maxwell, and two redacted documents. DOJ said this material "largely contains documents that have been previously leaked but never released in a formal capacity by the U.S. Government".
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General (with the Federal Bureau of Investigation)
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work) for the DOJ press release and letter; unverified for the attached records, which include material originally produced in U.S. v. Maxwell
entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs, press release 25-201
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (headless Chromium; justice.gov serves curl a bot-check interstitial). The release is titled "Attorney General Pamela Bondi Releases First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files" and dated Thursday, February 27, 2025, as press release number 25-201 ("Updated February 27, 2025"). It says the Attorney General, "in conjunction with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), declassified and publicly released files", and that DOJ "intends to release the remaining documents upon review and redaction to protect the identities of Epstein's victims".
Linked files (all on justice.gov/ag/media/<id>/dl):
- the AG's letter (1391331)
- "A. Evidence List" (1391271)
- "B. Flight Log_Released in U.S. v. Maxwell" plus Parts 1-6
- "C. Contact Book_Redacted" (1391321, about 19.4 MB)
- "D. Masseuse List_Redacted" (1391326)
Sampled files returned HTTP 200 application/pdf, with Last-Modified dates of 28 Feb 2025.
The stated authority is declassification by the AG with the FBI. This release predates the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The Epstein Library now also lists this material as "First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files" under DOJ Disclosures (https://www.justice.gov/epstein/doj-disclosures/first-phase-declassified-epstein-files), as four EFTA-renumbered PDFs (EFTA02846457 to EFTA02846673). The original press-release attachments and the library copies could diverge, so both URLs are worth watching.
Redaction: two attachments are labelled "_Redacted". No further redaction policy is stated on the release page.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.justice.gov/legalpolicies says "Unless otherwise indicated, information on Department of Justice websites is in the public domain". That is site-wide, and the attached records were not created by DOJ itself, so their status is unverified. I did not check the contents of the attachments.

entries.title: Eurostat Crime and Criminal Justice Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official statistics on police-recorded offences, persons brought into the criminal justice system, prisoners, and justice personnel across EU member states, collected jointly with UNODC.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (page title "Database - Crime and criminal justice - Eurostat"). Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) licenses its content under CC BY 4.0. The joint Eurostat-UNODC collection, mentioned in the description, comes from Eurostat's usual metadata and was not checked here. API and bulk access go through Eurostat's general dissemination services.

entries.title: FBI Crime Data Explorer (UCR / NIBRS)
entries.description: The FBI's portal for Uniform Crime Reporting Program data — incident-based NIBRS crime data, summary estimates, arrests, hate crime, expanded homicide, and law-enforcement employee data — at national, state, and agency level.
entries.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Criminal Justice Information Services Division

access.auth_note: The Crime Data API is referenced from the downloads page; its key requirements were not checked.

coverage.spatial: United States (national, state, and reporting-agency level)

entries.attribution: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, Crime Data Explorer
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200; the root redirects to /LATEST/webapp/#/pages/home and only renders with JavaScript. In headless Chromium, the Documents & Downloads page offers CSV downloads ("Incident-based data by state, summary data estimates, and data about other specific topics") and says "Data are also available via the Crime Data API". It notes the UCR Program provided updated 2025 data in August 2026. The API's auth terms were not confirmed. Agency participation in NIBRS varies by year, so coverage is uneven; that comes from FBI's own documentation and is not stated on the pages checked.

entries.title: Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database (IDB)
entries.description: Case-level data on civil case and criminal defendant filings and terminations in the U.S. district courts, plus bankruptcy and appellate court cases, maintained by the Federal Judicial Center with the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts.

coverage.spatial: United States (federal district, bankruptcy, and appellate courts)

entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page says the FJC, "under a working arrangement with the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AOUSC)", provides public access to the IDB, which holds civil and criminal district-court filings and terminations plus bankruptcy and appellate case information "from 1970 to the present". Download formats and the update cadence weren't checked; cadence is recorded as irregular until a steward confirms it.

entries.title: data.police.uk — Crime and Policing Open Data
entries.description: Open street-level crime, outcome, and stop-and-search data for England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, plus police force and neighbourhood information and police annual data requirement (ADR) returns, available as CSV downloads and an API.
entries.publisher: Home Office (United Kingdom), with police forces of England, Wales, and Northern Ireland

coverage.spatial: England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (street level, anonymised locations)

entries.attribution: data.police.uk, contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The site calls itself "the site for open data about crime and policing in England, Wales and Northern Ireland", with street-level crime, outcome, and stop-and-search downloads in CSV and an API. It states "All the data on this site is made available under the Open Government Licence v3.0". Several things come from the site's usual description and were not checked here: that the Home Office is the publisher, the monthly cadence, the rolling archive span, and json from the API.

entries.title: UNODC Data Portal
entries.description: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime's statistical portal covering intentional homicide, trafficking, prison populations, corruption, and access-to-justice indicators across UN member states.
entries.publisher: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
entries.license: unverified — data.unodc.org states no data licence; its footer links only the UN website terms (personal, non-commercial use); no Creative Commons licence found
entries.notes:
Verified reachable this session (HTTP 200, redirects to data.unodc.org). Seeded as this vertical's first international (non-US) source per operator request to seed the new verticals international-first.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the earlier CC-BY-3.0 IGO label is not supported. data.unodc.org states no data licence; its footer links the UN copyright page (https://www.un.org/en/about-us/copyright) and UNODC's legal notice (https://www.unodc.org/unodc/legal.html), which allows downloading and copying "for the User's personal, non-commercial use, without any right to resell or redistribute them or to compile or create derivative works therefrom". That is a website-content licence, not a stated data licence. An older dataUNODC terms page, seen only in a search snippet, said the data "may be copied freely, duplicated, and further distributed provided that UNODC is cited as the reference"; it now redirects to the portal home and could not be read.

entries.title: U.S. Sentencing Commission Datafiles
entries.description: The Sentencing Commission's annual case-level datafiles on sentences imposed in federal criminal cases — individual offenders, organizational defendants, and special collections — with identifiers removed, for quantitative research on federal sentencing.
entries.attribution: United States Sentencing Commission, Commission Datafiles
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes the datafiles as excluding identifiers and providing "fiscal year data for researchers interested in studying federal sentencing practices". It lists Individuals, Organizations, Special Collections, and Special Reports datafiles, and says they are also distributed through ICPSR. The SAS/SPSS formats come from the Commission's usual distribution and were not checked file by file. The USSC is an independent agency in the judicial branch.
